text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Visiting Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad is expected today to lay a foundation stone at a proposed site for the Blantyre City Centre Hotel and another for a housing project before meeting representatives of the business community in Blantyre.

- Director of Public Prosecution Kamudoni Nyasulu said on Wednesday a jury was not necessary in the ongoing K137 ($9 million) million fraud case involving former Malawi President Kamuzu Banda and three of his party's prominent members.
- Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) president Thomas Banda said on Wednesday that government had finally agreed to hold talks with the union to end the workers' four week nationwide strike.

- Government union leader for southern Malawi Thomas Mwafongo was on Wednesday rushed from a police cell to hospital after a heavy beating by police during a 24-hour ordeal since his arrest on Tuesday.
- Director of Public Prosecutions Kamudoni Nyasulu on Wednesday apologised for telling defendants in the K137 million fraud case that they would be tried by a jury.

- National Soccer coach Reuben Malola has been fired following an eight-hour-long meeting on Wednesday by the Malawi National Council of Sports which decided to relieve him of his duties due to poor performance by the Malawi national soccer team.
- The country's biggest conglomerate, Press Corporation has re-engaged Charles Freyer as its chief executive after he vacated the post in 1992.
